title: General multidimensional CompOSE reader/writer: read all T x Yq x nb cells, arbitrary Nadd
document_type: DESIGN (no implementation; implementation is the next phase)
objective: Extend the native CompOSE reader/writer beyond the single cold T=0 slice to support the full CompOSE multidimensional table format: all T x Yq x nb thermo cells, arbitrary Nadd (>=0) extra-quantity columns, and a 3D tensor data model that does not break the existing cold-slice production path.

current_state.data_model: eos_data_t (compose_eos_types.f90) stores a 1D cold slice: q(7,n) over nb, q_extra(n) for a single extra quantity, nadd as a single integer for the whole table. nT/nYq/t_axis/yq_axis/selected_iT/selected_iYq carry the axes metadata but only the selected cold slice is materialized.
reader_constraints: compose_eos_io.f90 line 130-132: rejects multi-point T or Yq axes or T!=0
compose_eos_io.f90 line 195-197: thermo rows must match a single selected_iT/selected_iYq
compose_eos_io.f90 line 213: thermo row width must match Nadd
downstream_consumers_of_the_1D_model: M3-M6 reconstruction (GPPVA/SPG coupling extraction, splicing, causal-complete, Maxwell)
fill_density_gap / reconstruct-master / causal-complete / match-core / maxwell-transition (Fortran app commands)
Python api.py read_compose / write_compose / from_internal_directory / write_internal_directory

D1_data_model_extension.decision: Add a 3D tensor view q_full(nT, nYq, n) and an extra-quantity tensor q_extra_full(nadd_max, nT, nYq, n) to eos_data_t, ALLOCATABLE and unallocated by default. The existing q(7,n) / q_extra(n) / nadd fields remain and continue to hold the selected slice (the cold slice by default). A selector selects_iT/selected_iYq materializes q/q_extra from q_full/q_extra_full for the chosen slice.
D1_data_model_extension.rationale: Preserves the cold-slice surface API (q, q_extra, nadd) so M3-M6 and the app commands keep working unchanged. The tensor view is opt-in: readers that only need the cold slice (the current EOS390 path) never allocate it.
D1_data_model_extension.risk: Memory: a full 3D table is nT*nYq*n*7 doubles; for n~1000, nT~50, nYq~20 this is ~5.6 GB. Mitigation: the tensor is allocated only when the table is genuinely multidimensional (nT>1 or nYq>1) AND the caller requests the full view; cold-slice reads never allocate it.

D2_reader_relaxation_order.decision: Relax the reader in three independent, gated steps, each with its own unit tests, so a regression in one step does not invalidate the others:
steps: Step 1 (Nadd relaxation): remove the nadd<=1 bound (line 207) and the width check (line 213) when nadd>=0; store q_extra as a 1D array of size n*nadd (row-major, nadd varies fastest) for the cold slice. Requires q_extra(n) -> q_extra(n, nadd_max) or a separate q_extra_block. Backward compatible for Nadd in {0,1}.
Step 2 (multi-point Yq axis): allow nYq>1 while keeping nT==1 (T=0); read all Yq thermo rows into q_full(1, nYq, n). The cold slice (selected_iYq) still materializes q(7,n).

Step 3 (multi-point T axis): allow nT>1; read all T x Yq rows into q_full(nT, nYq, n). Reject only non-cold T>0 for the slice materialization when a cold-slice consumer is attached (M3-M6), but keep the full tensor for multidim consumers.

D3_slice_materialization_API.decision: Add a Fortran subroutine select_slice(eos, iT, iYq, status) that copies q_full(iT,iYq,:) into q(:,n) and q_extra_full(:,iT,iYq,:) into q_extra(n, :). The Python side exposes this as EOSData.select_slice(iT, iYq) returning a 1D cold-slice EOSData view.
D3_slice_materialization_API.rationale: M3-M6 and app commands consume the 1D q/q_extra; select_slice bridges the tensor to the 1D surface without changing their call sites.

D4_writer_extension.decision: write_internal_csv writes the full q_full/q_extra_full when allocated, plus the axes; write_compose emits the multidim eos.t/eos.yq/eos.thermo with all cells. A legacy flag preserves the 1D cold-slice write for backward compatibility.
D4_writer_extension.rationale: Round-trip losslessness requires writing all cells, not just the selected slice.

downstream_impact_analysis.M3_M6_cold_slice_path: UNAFFECTED if D1/D3 hold: the 1D q/q_extra/nadd fields are still populated for the selected cold slice; M3-M6 never see q_full unless they opt in.
downstream_impact_analysis.app_commands: UNAFFECTED for cold-slice inputs; a new command 'read-multidim' or an option to 'read' (--full-tensor) opts into the tensor.
downstream_impact_analysis.tests: test_m10_generic_axes.py rejection tests (test_multi_point_T_axis_is_rejected, test_multi_point_Yq_axis_is_rejected, test_nonzero_T_slice_is_rejected) become acceptance tests for the relaxed reader; they must be rewritten to assert successful read + correct cell counts, not rejection.

open_questions_for_user: Q1: Is there a real CompOSE 2D/3D table the EOS390 pipeline must ingest (not just the cold slice)? If yes, providing one (even a small synthetic one in the standard format) would let phase 2-5 be validated against real data rather than synthetic tables.
Q2: The memory bound (D1 risk) assumes the largest table the pipeline will see. What is the expected max (nT, nYq, n)? This decides whether q_full should be memory-mapped or in-core.
Q3: Should select_slice copy (safe, doubles memory transiently) or reference (zero-copy but lifetime-coupled to q_full)? Default: copy, matching the existing q/q_extra semantics.
next_node_recommendation: E390-10B design is complete. Implementation (phases 1-5) is unblocked and can proceed in the next session; phase 6 (real-data validation) is blocked by E390-00. Recommend starting phase 1 (D1 data model, no reader change) as the lowest-risk first step, with a synthetic Nadd=2 table test.
